Kessa called out for her mother, but her voice was swallowed by the roar of the water pouring over the broken gate. Inside, she found the mill floor already flooding, sacks of flour split open and dissolving into pale sludge. Her mother, Ilsa, was on the upper platform, struggling to free a length of rope tangled around the main support beam. "Kessa!" Ilsa called down.

input: Frost crept across the greenhouse panes as Solveig checked the thermometer for the third time that hour, worry creasing her forehead at how fast the temperature had dropped since sunset.
target: Cold air seeps through glass as Solveig anxiously monitors the plummeting thermometer.

input: An unexpected cold snap had rolled in early, threatening the seedlings she'd spent all spring nurturing.
target: A chill wind threatens fragile seedlings nurtured through spring.

input:
Her farmhand, Percival, hauled in another armful of old blankets, draping them carefully over the most vulnerable rows of tomato starts near the door. "Heater's running full blast," he said, breath visible even inside the greenhouse now. "Not sure it's enough on its own tonight." Solveig nodded grimly and grabbed a stack of empty buckets, filling them with water from the hose bib and setting them strategically between the rows.
Known appearances: Heater (The Heater is a large, robust man with graying hair and a thick wool coat.); hose (Solveig has shoulder-length hair tied back, wears a warm jacket and long pants, and has a sturdy build.)
target: Solveig and Percival work to protect tomato starts from the cold.

input: "Water holds heat longer than air," she said.
target: Heat rises as water retains warmth.

input: "It'll radiate out slowly overnight and might buy us a few extra degrees where it matters most." Percival finished draping the last blanket and grabbed a battery-powered lantern, checking the thermometer readings at the far end of the greenhouse where the cold seemed to be settling worst.
target: Night falls as Percival checks the greenhouse temperature, securing blankets against the chill.

input: "Corner's already at thirty-four," he called back. "We might lose the peppers over there no matter what we do." Solveig hurried over with two more water buckets, setting them close to the struggling pepper starts before straightening up and surveying the dimly lit rows one final time. "Then we watch it through the night," she said. "I'm not losing this crop to one bad cold front without a fight."
target: Pepper starts struggle in dimly lit greenhouse as Solveig sets up buckets.

input: Heat shimmered off the kiln's brick walls as Thaddeus checked the pyrometric cones through the small peephole, judging by their slow bending exactly how much longer the firing needed to run.
target: Thaddeus peers into the kiln, watching cones bend slowly.

input: The wood-fired kiln had been burning steadily for eighteen hours already, and everyone on the crew was running on fumes and strong coffee. His firing partner, Wilhelmina, fed another split log into the firebox, sweat streaking through the ash already coating her forearms. "Cone six is starting to droop," she said, squinting through her own peephole on the opposite side.
target: Wood-fired kiln burns steadily; Wilhelmina feeds logs, monitoring cone six.

input: "Maybe another hour if we keep the temperature climbing steady." Thaddeus nodded and adjusted the damper slightly, coaxing a bit more draft through the chamber without risking a temperature spike that could crack the pots inside.
target: Thaddeus monitors the temperature, adjusting the damper carefully.

input: "Keep feeding it small and steady," he said. "We rush this now and three weeks of glazing work goes up in smoke." Wilhelmina wiped her brow with the back of her wrist and reached for another log, stacking it carefully near the firebox door for the next feed. The two of them fell into the familiar rhythm they'd built over a dozen firings together, barely needing words anymore to coordinate the work.
target: Wilhelmina stacks logs while wiping sweat, emphasizing urgency.

input: By the time cone seven finally slumped fully at dawn, both of them were exhausted but grinning, watching the first hints of sunrise catch the kiln's shimmering heat above the chimney.
target: Dawn breaks as the kiln's heat glimmers; they grin from exhaustion.

input: "Told you we'd make it," Thaddeus said, already beginning the long process of sealing the kiln for its slow cooldown.
target: Thaddeus smirks as he starts sealing the kiln.

input:
Felt hammers clicked softly against strings as Rosalind worked her way up the keyboard, tuning fork ringing faintly against her wrist between each careful adjustment. The old upright had sat untouched in the church basement for years, and half its strings had drifted badly out of tune. Her apprentice, Callahan, sat nearby with a notepad, logging each string's measurement as she called it out, occasionally wincing at a particularly sour note before she corrected it. "That's the fourth string that's snapped this week," he said.
Known appearances: Callahan (Callahan has short brown hair, wears a white shirt and khaki pants, and has a lean build.); Rosalind (Rosalind wore a simple blouse and trousers, her hair tied back in a practical bun.)
target: Rosalind tunes an old piano while Callahan records, both focused and determined.

input:
"Are these just old, or is something wrong with the whole piano?" Rosalind paused, resting her tuning lever against the pinblock, and considered the question seriously before answering.
Known appearances: Rosalind (Rosalind wore a simple blouse and trousers, her hair tied back in a practical bun.)
target: Rosalind contemplates the piano's condition, brow furrowed.

input: "Both, probably," she said. "Age makes strings brittle, and a piano left in a damp basement for a decade doesn't help matters much either." She resumed her slow climb up the register.
target: A pianist ascends the keys slowly, contemplating the wear and tear on an instrument.

input:
Callahan flipped to a fresh page and kept logging, occasionally plucking a string himself to compare its pitch against Rosalind's reference tone.
Known appearances: Callahan (Callahan has short brown hair, wears a white shirt and khaki pants, and has a lean build.); Rosalind (Rosalind wore a simple blouse and trousers, her hair tied back in a practical bun.)
target: Callahan writes while comparing a plucked piano string to Rosalind's reference tone.

input:
"This one sounds right to me," he offered hesitantly, and Rosalind checked it against her fork before nodding in agreement, letting him log it without correction.
Known appearances: Rosalind (Rosalind wore a simple blouse and trousers, her hair tied back in a practical bun.)
target: Rosalind checks the string against her tuning fork, then nods in agreement as Callahan logs it.

input:
By the time she reached the top octave, the basement's single overhead light had dimmed twice from a flickering bulb, and Rosalind finally sat back to play a slow scale across the freshly tuned keys. "Not perfect," she said, "but it'll hold through Sunday's service, which is all we need right now."
Known appearances: Rosalind (Rosalind wore a simple blouse and trousers, her hair tied back in a practical bun.)
target: Dim light flickers as Rosalind sits at the piano, playing a slow scale.

input: Cold morning air bit at Fennimore's ears as he climbed the ladder propped against the old apple tree, loppers in hand, breath fogging with each careful exhale. Winter pruning had to happen before the sap started rising, and this orchard had forty more trees waiting after this one. His daughter, Marguerite, home from college for the weekend, held the ladder steady from below, occasionally pointing out branches he'd missed from her lower vantage point. "That one crossing through the middle," she called up.
target: Winter morning; Fennimore climbs ladder, prunes apple tree, daughter assists below.

input: "You always say those are the first ones to go." Fennimore squinted up into the tangled canopy and found the branch she meant, angling the loppers carefully before making the cut in one clean motion.
target: Tangled branches yield to careful pruning.

input: "Good eye," he said, tossing the severed branch down into the growing pile beside the ladder's base. "You've been paying attention all these years after all." Marguerite laughed and dragged the pile of branches toward the burn area at the orchard's edge, her breath visible in the cold air as she worked.
target: Branches pile up as Marguerite laughs, tossing another branch into the growing stack.

input: "Hard not to, growing up climbing these same trees every summer," she said.
target: Memories flood as she gazes up at familiar trees from her childhood.

input: "Though I never thought I'd miss the smell of cut branches this much." By midafternoon they'd worked through six trees together, the rhythm of pruning and hauling settling into something almost meditative in the crisp winter light.
target: Winter light casts a crisp glow as the rhythmic work continues.

input: Fennimore climbed down from the last tree of the day and surveyed their progress with quiet satisfaction, already looking forward to next weekend's continuation.
target: Fennimore stands beneath the trees, smiling at a day’s work accomplished.

input:
Bubbles trailed upward past Bronwyn's mask as she descended along the anchor line, the wreck's rusted hull emerging slowly out of the hazy blue below. Twenty years underwater had softened the old cargo ship's silhouette, coral now claiming what had once been steel and rivets.
Known appearances: Bronwyn (Bronwyn wears a diving mask and snorkel, with short hair and a slim build.)
target: Bronwyn descends, bubbles trailing, hull of old wreck emerging.

input:
Her dive buddy, Anwar, signaled from a few feet away, checking his gauge before pointing toward the ship's broken bow section where a school of silver fish scattered at their approach.
Known appearances: Anwar (Anwar has short brown hair, wears a diving suit, and has a lean build.)
target: Anwar signals, points towards the ship’s bow as fish scatter.

input:
Bronwyn nodded through her regulator and followed, careful to keep her fins clear of the fragile coral growth along the hull.
Known appearances: Bronwyn (Bronwyn wears a diving mask and snorkel, with short hair and a slim build.)
target: Bronwyn dives alongside the ship, eyes focused, mask obscuring her face.

input: They drifted along the deck's edge together, flashlight beams cutting through the gloom of the ship's open cargo holds, revealing shapes too dark to identify from the surface briefing.
target: Flashlight beams illuminate dark cargo hold shapes as they walk the deck's edge.

input:
Anwar paused near an old ship's wheel, still miraculously intact, and gestured for Bronwyn to come take a closer look.
Known appearances: Bronwyn (Bronwyn wears a diving mask and snorkel, with short hair and a slim build.); Anwar (Anwar has short brown hair, wears a diving suit, and has a lean build.)
target: Anwar points towards the old ship's wheel; Bronwyn approaches curiously.

input:
Bronwyn hovered beside him, adjusting her buoyancy carefully as she studied the corroded wheel now home to a small cluster of anemones swaying gently in the current. She checked her air gauge, tapping Anwar's shoulder and holding up ten fingers to signal their remaining bottom time before the ascent. Anwar nodded and took one last photo of the wheel before they began working their way back toward the anchor line, ascending slowly to let their bodies adjust to the changing pressure. By the time they broke the surface, both were grinning behind their masks, already trading excited gestures about what they'd seen below.
Known appearances: Bronwyn (Bronwyn wears a diving mask and snorkel, with short hair and a slim build.); Anwar (Anwar has short brown hair, wears a diving suit, and has a lean build.)
target: Bronwyn and Anwar ascend from the underwater wreck, faces lit with excitement.

input: Metal rang against metal as Guinevere shaped the glowing horseshoe on her portable anvil, sparks scattering across the barn's packed dirt floor with each precise hammer strike. The old mare waited patiently in her stall nearby, already accustomed to the ritual after a decade of regular visits. The barn's owner, Peregrine, held the mare's lead rope loosely, running a calming hand along her neck whenever she shifted her weight. "She's been favoring that front left again," he said.
target: Guinevere hammers a horseshoe while Peregrine calms the mare.

input: "Nothing dramatic, just a little hesitant on the turns lately." Guinevere quenched the shoe in a bucket of water with a sharp hiss of steam and carried it over, checking its shape against the mare's hoof before making any final adjustments.
target: Guinevere quenches the glowing horseshoe in water, steam rising, then checks its fit against the mare's hoof.

input: "Let's take a look," she said, lifting the hoof gently and examining the frog and sole for any obvious signs of bruising or infection. "Nothing serious here," Guinevere said after a careful inspection, setting the hoof back down and reaching for her rasp.
target: A gentle examination of a hoof, searching for injuries.

input: "Might just be the angle wearing unevenly. I'll adjust the trim a bit this time and we'll see if that helps her turns." Peregrine nodded, visibly relieved at the reassurance.
target: Uneven wear causes concern; relief follows a proposed solution.

input: Guinevere worked methodically through the trim and fitting, the mare standing calm and still under Peregrine's steady hand the entire time.
target: Guinevere meticulously trims the mare as Peregrine holds it steady.

input: When the final shoe was nailed and clinched, Guinevere straightened up and stepped back to check the mare's stance, satisfied with the level, even set of all four feet.
target: A stable, mare stands with her stance checked after shoeing.

input:
Chalk dust hung in the air as Zephyrine studied the overhanging route, tracing the sequence of holds with her eyes before chalking up for another attempt. The gym buzzed with the usual evening crowd, ropes swinging and climbers calling encouragement across the padded floor. Her climbing partner, Osei, stood belay-ready at the base of the wall, rope looped through his device as he watched her chalk her hands one final time. "You had it last try," he called up. "Just commit to the deadpoint instead of hesitating at the crux." Zephyrine nodded and stepped onto the wall, moving smoothly through the opening sequence before pausing at the same crux move that had shut her down twice already.
Known appearances: Osei (Osei has short dark hair, wears a black t-shirt and gym shorts, and has a lean build.)
target: Zephyrine chocks up, eyes focused on the crux move.

input: She took a breath, then lunged for the sloping hold above, fingers barely catching the edge before her feet cut loose from the wall.
target: She leaps upward, face set in determination, fingers clutching the edge.

input:
Osei held the rope steady, watching her feet scramble to find purchase again as she hung by fingertips from the small hold.
Known appearances: Osei (Osei has short dark hair, wears a black t-shirt and gym shorts, and has a lean build.)
target: Osei hangs precariously, eyes focused intently.

input: "You've got it, reset your feet," he called, keeping his voice calm despite the tension in his grip on the belay device.
target: Tension hangs as he guides someone to reset their stance.

input: Zephyrine found a foothold and pulled through the final moves to the anchor, clipping in with a triumphant shout that drew a few claps from nearby climbers.
target: Climber reaches peak, clips in triumphantly.

input:
She lowered slowly to the ground, grinning and shaking out her forearms while Osei coiled the rope and grinned back at her.
Known appearances: Osei (Osei has short dark hair, wears a black t-shirt and gym shorts, and has a lean build.)
target: She lowers to the ground, grinning; Osei coils the rope, smiling back.

input:
Red safelight cast everything in a dim crimson glow as Ottoline slid the exposed paper into the developer tray, watching the image slowly bloom into visibility beneath the liquid's surface. The darkroom smelled of chemicals and old habit, a ritual she'd kept alive long after most had gone fully digital. Her nephew, Barnaby, leaned over the next tray with a pair of tongs, waiting nervously for his own first print to develop. "Is it supposed to take this long?" he whispered, as if speaking too loudly might somehow ruin the process.
Known appearances: Barnaby (Barnaby has short brown hair, wears a white lab coat over a blue shirt, and has a slender build.); Ottoline (Wearing glasses, mid-length auburn hair tied back, slender build.)
target: Ottoline watches as Barnaby waits nervously by the developer tray, the dim red light casting shadows on their faces.

input:
Ottoline smiled in the red light and used her own tongs to lift her print, letting the excess developer drip back into the tray.
Known appearances: Ottoline (Wearing glasses, mid-length auburn hair tied back, slender build.)
target: Ottoline smiles as she lifts her print, letting developer drip.

input:
"Patience is half of this craft," she said. "Rush it and you'll either underdevelop the shadows or blow out everything trying to force it." Barnaby's own print began emerging beneath the surface, faint shapes resolving slowly into the portrait he'd shot of his dog that morning.
Known appearances: Barnaby (Barnaby has short brown hair, wears a white lab coat over a blue shirt, and has a slender build.)
target: Barnaby watches his developing print, patience etched on his face.

input:
He gasped quietly and reached to pull it too early, but Ottoline caught his wrist gently before he could disturb the developing chemistry.
Known appearances: Ottoline (Wearing glasses, mid-length auburn hair tied back, slender build.)
target: Ottoline gently restrains him as he reaches out.

input: "Not yet," she said, timing it against the small clock ticking on the counter.
target: She watches the ticking clock, her expression patient.

input:
"Thirty more seconds, then we stop it and fix it properly." Barnaby waited, practically vibrating with anticipation, until Ottoline finally nodded and helped him transfer the print to the stop bath.
Known appearances: Barnaby (Barnaby has short brown hair, wears a white lab coat over a blue shirt, and has a slender build.); Ottoline (Wearing glasses, mid-length auburn hair tied back, slender build.)
target: Barnaby and Ottoline work together, eyes focused intently on the print in the stop bath.

input: Molten glass glowed orange at the end of the blowpipe as Cassiopeia rotated it steadily over the workbench, gravity pulling the gather into a slow, even bulb beneath her practiced hands.
target: Glassblower shapes molten glass into a bulb.

input: The furnace roared behind her, its heat pressing against her face even from several feet away. Her studio partner, Thorsten, stood ready with the jacks, watching her rhythm closely so he'd know exactly when to step in and help shape the piece. "Looking good," he said.
target: Furnace flames roar; partner watches intently.

input: "Nice and even, no cold spots forming on that side yet." Cassiopeia carried the glowing bulb to the marver and rolled it smooth against the steel table, cooling the surface just enough to control the shape without losing the workability underneath.
target: Cassiopeia smooths the glowing bulb on the steel marver, eyes focused.

input: "Get the blowpipe ready," she said.
target: She gestures towards the blowpipe, her face serious.

input: "I want to puff it before it stiffens up too much to move." Thorsten passed her a fresh breath of air through the tube while she rotated the pipe, watching the bulb expand slowly into a rounder, more defined form under the combined heat and pressure.
target: A pipe slowly inflates as Thorsten supplies air, the user watches intently.

input: Sweat beaded on both their foreheads despite the studio's open bay doors letting in the cooler evening air. By the time the piece was fully shaped and ready for the annealer, both of them stepped back to admire the swirling blue and amber pattern trapped within the glass. "That one's a keeper," Thorsten said, already reaching for the tools to start the next piece.
target: Cool evening air fails to dissipate sweat as artists admire their glasswork.

input: Morning mist still clung to the field as Persimmon raised her gloved fist, the young hawk shifting its weight and studying the open grass beyond with sharp, focused eyes. Months of patient training had brought them to this first real free flight, and her stomach was tighter than she wanted to admit.
target: Morning mist envelops the field; Persimmon clenches her fist, hawk watches intently.

input: Her mentor, Ezekiel, stood a short distance away with the lure ready, watching the hawk's body language for any sign of hesitation before nodding to Persimmon.
target: Mentor Ezekiel signals Persimmon as she prepares to cast, hawk poised for flight.

input: "She's locked on," he said quietly.
target: He whispers, eyes focused intently.

input: "Release when you're ready, and trust the training." Persimmon took a slow breath and opened her fist, and the hawk launched into the misty air with a powerful downstroke, climbing before banking wide across the field toward Ezekiel's outstretched lure.
target: A hawk soars into the misty sky from a slow release.

input:
She watched with her heart in her throat, half-certain the bird would simply keep flying and never look back. The hawk closed the distance fast, talons extending as it struck the lure cleanly and settled onto the grass, feathers ruffling with satisfaction over the successful catch. Ezekiel knelt slowly, offering a small piece of meat as reward while keeping his movements calm and unhurried. Persimmon jogged over, relief flooding through her as she watched the hawk feed contentedly under Ezekiel's steady hand.
Known appearances: Ezekiel knelt (Ezekiel knelt with weathered hands, wearing a worn leather jacket and jeans, his dark hair tied back.)
target: Hawk feeds contentedly; Ezekiel offers meat calmly.

input: "She came back," she said, voice cracking slightly with emotion. "I really wasn't sure she would." Ezekiel smiled and nodded toward the glove. "Now you get to be the one she comes back to."
target: Voice trembling, she recounts a near-miss reunion.

input: Cool damp air settled over Guillermina's shoulders as she descended the stone steps into the aging cave, headlamp cutting through the darkness toward the long rows of wheels resting on wooden shelves. The cave had held a steady fifty-two degrees for two hundred years, long before anyone thought to measure it.
target: Cool air greets Guillermina as she enters the ancient cave with her headlamp illuminating rows of wheels.

input: Her cellar hand, Ottavia, followed close behind carrying a brushing kit, ready to tend to the wheels that needed their monthly rind maintenance.
target: Ottavia carries a brushing kit, following closely behind, ready to clean the wheels.

input: "Row three's looking a little dry again," she said, running gloved fingers along one wheel's crusted surface.
target: Crusted wheel surface inspected, gloves worn, concern evident.

input: "Might need another brine wipe this week." Guillermina knelt to inspect the wheel Ottavia mentioned, turning it gently to check the rind's development on all sides before setting it back precisely where it had been resting.
target: Guillermina inspects a wheel of cheese, checking its brine coating.

input: "Good catch," she said. "Humidity's been fighting us all month. Let's get the whole row brined before it spreads." Ottavia set down her kit and began mixing the brine solution in a small bucket, the salty smell mixing with the cave's earthy must as she worked. Guillermina moved down the row methodically, flipping wheels and checking each one's progress with the practiced efficiency of someone who'd done this thousands of times.
target: Ottavia mixes brine while Guillermina inspects wheels, determined expressions.

input: By the time they'd finished the row, both women's hands were pruned and cold from the damp work, but satisfied with the wheels' steady progress toward readiness. "Another six weeks on this batch," Guillermina said, climbing back toward the stairs. "Then we finally get to taste if all this fuss was worth it."
target: Hands red from scrubbing, faces set with determination as they survey the rows of wheels nearing completion.

input:
Coals glowed white-hot in the forge as Ottokar pumped the bellows steadily, watching the steel bar deep in the fire shift from orange toward the color he needed for the next fold. Sweat ran freely down his back despite the open doors letting in the autumn air. His apprentice, Seraphina, stood at the anvil with tongs ready, having spent the morning learning to read the metal's color the way Ottokar had drilled into her for weeks. "That looks close," she said.
Known appearances: Ottokar (Ottokar has graying hair, wears a leather apron, and has a muscular build.)
target: Ottokar pumps bellows, watching steel glow; Seraphina stands ready.

input:
"Is it ready to pull?" Ottokar squinted at the glowing steel and shook his head slightly.
Known appearances: Ottokar (Ottokar has graying hair, wears a leather apron, and has a muscular build.)
target: Ottokar squints at the glowing steel, shaking his head.

input:
"Not quite, give it another thirty seconds," he said. "Pull it too cool and the fold won't weld properly, you'll just be hammering two pieces that never truly joined." Seraphina nodded and watched the fire carefully, resisting the urge to reach for the tongs before he gave the signal. When Ottokar finally nodded, she pulled the bar free in one smooth motion and set it on the anvil for him to strike.
Known appearances: Ottokar (Ottokar has graying hair, wears a leather apron, and has a muscular build.)
target: Ottokar instructs Seraphina as she watches the fire, muscles tensed, ready to pull the metal bar.

input:
Ottokar's hammer rang out in steady, measured blows, folding the glowing steel back on itself with practiced precision as sparks scattered across the shop floor.
Known appearances: Ottokar (Ottokar has graying hair, wears a leather apron, and has a muscular build.)
target: Ottokar hammers steel, sparks fly.

input: "This is the part that actually makes the steel strong," he said between strikes.
target: A blacksmith strikes the glowing steel, face set in determination.

input: "Everything before this was just getting it ready."
target: Preparations complete; anticipation builds.

input: Spray cans rattled as Ximena shook another color before laying down a broad sweep of blue across the community center's brick wall, the outline of the mural already taking shape after weeks of planning.
target: Ximena paints a broad sweep of blue on the community center wall.

input:
Traffic hummed past on the street behind her, occasional honks of encouragement from passing cars. Her mural partner, Desmond, worked on the scaffolding above, filling in the upper section with careful strokes of a paint roller, pausing occasionally to check his section against the reference sketch taped nearby. "The color's reading a little too dark up here," he called down.
Known appearances: Desmond (Desmond wears a hard hat, safety vest, and carries a paint roller. Medium build.)
target: Desmond paints on scaffolding while traffic hums below.

input: "Might need to blend in more of that lighter blue." Ximena stepped back to survey both sections together, comparing the transition zone where their two areas would eventually meet.
target: Ximena steps back, examining the lighter blue section.

input: "You're right, let's mix a batch to bridge it," she said, already reaching for her palette to test a new combination against the wall.
target: She mixes colors, determinedly testing a new palette against the wall.

input:
Desmond climbed partway down the scaffolding to compare colors directly, holding a test swatch up against both sections until they found a shade that blended seamlessly.
Known appearances: Desmond (Desmond wears a hard hat, safety vest, and carries a paint roller. Medium build.)
target: Desmond compares paint swatches on scaffolding, focused and meticulous.

input: "That's it," he said, climbing back up with the new mixture to continue his section. By sunset, the mural's central figures had emerged fully from the brick, vibrant against the neighborhood's usual gray backdrop, drawing a small crowd of curious onlookers. Ximena capped her spray can and stepped back to take in the full piece, exhausted but proud of what they'd built together over the past month.
target: Vibrant mural emerges at sunset, drawing a crowd.

input: Waves crashed hard against the rocks below as Isolde climbed the lighthouse's spiral stairs, storm winds rattling the old glass panes with each violent gust.
target: Stormy winds and crashing waves accompany Isolde's ascent up the lighthouse.

input:
The automated light had failed an hour ago, and the fishing boats still out past the point needed it working before the storm worsened further. Her radio crackled with updates from her assistant, Percy, stationed below at the generator room, working to diagnose the electrical fault that had knocked out the primary system. "Backup circuit's fried too," his voice crackled through the static.
Known appearances: Percy (Percy has short brown hair, wears a navy work uniform, and has a lean build.)
target: Darkening sea beyond the point; Percy frowns into the radio.

input: "You'll need to run the lamp manually until I can get it fixed." Isolde reached the lamp room, hands already moving to the manual crank mechanism she hadn't touched in years, muscle memory returning despite the disuse.
target: Isolde cranks the old lamp mechanism, determined expression.

input: She began turning it steadily, feeling the mechanism resist before slowly catching the familiar old rhythm.
target: A hand turns a mechanism, face focused with determination.

input: "Light's turning," she said into her radio, breathing hard from the effort of maintaining the crank's pace.
target: She breathes hard, cranking the generator as the lights flicker.

input:
"How long until you can get the backup running?" Percy's reply crackled back, thin and strained. "Give me twenty minutes, maybe less if this splice holds." Isolde kept cranking steadily, arms burning, watching through the rain-lashed glass as the beam swept its familiar arc across the churning black water. Somewhere out there, boats were counting on that light, and she wasn't about to let her arms give out before Percy finished his work.
Known appearances: Percy (Percy has short brown hair, wears a navy work uniform, and has a lean build.)
target: Rain pelts glass as Isolde strains, watching light beam sweep dark waters.

input:
Sawdust crunched underfoot as Radomir worked the boning knife along the joint with practiced precision, separating the cut cleanly while barely glancing down at his hands. Forty years behind this same counter had taught him exactly where every joint wanted to give. His son, Anatol, home for the summer before starting culinary school, watched from beside him, taking mental notes on the angle of the blade through each motion. "You never seem to think about it," he said.
Known appearances: Anatol (Anatol wore a casual shirt and jeans, with short brown hair.); Radomir (Radomir has graying hair, wears a chef's apron, and has a sturdy build.)
target: Radomir works the boning knife, eyes focused; son watches intently, learning.

input:
"How do your hands just know where to cut?" Radomir set the finished cut aside and reached for the next piece, considering the question while he worked.
Known appearances: Radomir (Radomir has graying hair, wears a chef's apron, and has a sturdy build.)
target: Radomir ponders his precise cuts, setting aside the latest piece.

input: "Same way your hands will know eventually," he said.
target: Hands will know eventually.

input: "Right now you're thinking through every step.
target: Thoughts swirl as he thinks through each careful step.

input:
One day you won't be thinking at all, you'll just be doing." Anatol picked up his own knife and attempted the same cut on a practice piece, moving slower and more deliberately than his father, checking the angle twice before committing to the stroke.
Known appearances: Anatol (Anatol wore a casual shirt and jeans, with short brown hair.)
target: Anatol carefully mimics his father’s cut, scrutinizing the angle.

input:
The cut came out slightly ragged along one edge, but structurally sound. Radomir inspected his son's work and gave an approving nod, setting both cuts side by side on the counter for comparison. "Not bad for someone who's been at this three weeks," he said. "Keep at it and by the time you leave for school, these hands will know plenty too."
Known appearances: Radomir (Radomir has graying hair, wears a chef's apron, and has a sturdy build.)
target: Radomir examines his son's work, nodding approvingly.

input:
Dust motes drifted through the beam of Cornelius's flashlight as he crawled beneath the old star projector, tracing a bundle of wiring toward the source of the intermittent short that had plagued the machine for weeks. The museum's evening show started in two hours, and half the winter constellations still flickered unpredictably.
Known appearances: Cornelius (Cornelius wore a faded work uniform, had short brown hair, and a lean build.)
target: Cornelius crawls beneath a projector, tracing wires while motes dance in flashlight beam.
